newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Real-life "Skippy" saves Australian from blaze.
newsitem.headline: Real-life "Skippy" saves Australian from blaze.

text.p: A small kangaroo saved an Australian farmer's life on Thursday, waking him up after a fire broke out in a house they shared in the outback.
In a rescue that mirrored the heroic deeds of Australian television's cult kangaroo star, Skippy, the knee-high marsupial used his tail to bang on the farmer's bedroom door to alert him.
"If the wallaby hadn't woken me up I would have been dead," Nigel Etherington told Reuters from his farm east of the western coast city of Perth. "I'm ecstatic."
A wallaby is a smaller cousin of the kangaroo.

Etherington said he rescued the wallaby on Wednesday night after it was hit by a car near his farm. He took the injured animal home, nursed it, left it to sleep on the floor of his bathroom and went to bed.
In the early hours of Thursday, an electrical fire broke out in a spare bedroom and the wallaby hopped into action.
What happened next was later dubbed "the Skippy alarm" by bemused firefighters who were called to the scene.
"It was rattling my bedroom door," Etherington said, adding that he opened the door to find the house choked with thick smoke. "I grabbed it and put it out on the front lawn."
Etherington, a volunteer firefighter, said he brought the fire under control with a hose before the local fire brigade arrived. He now plans to give the wallaby a home on his farm.
"It's the first time I've heard of anyone being saved by a kangaroo," said fire brigade chief Brad Hibble.
"Skippy" was a 1970s TV series starring a fictional kangaroo that routinely pulled off miraculous rescues and became Australia's answer to Hollywood's "Lassie" and "Flipper".
